html:
Dionysius I was the tyrant of Syracuse in Sicily from 405 to 367 BCE. He made it the strongest Greek city in the west, and ancient writers remembered him as the model of a cruel, suspicious despot.

He rose to power when Carthage invaded Sicily and took one Greek city after another. Elected general in the crisis, he made himself sole ruler. Then he spent almost forty years at war:

  • He turned the island of Ortygia into a fortress for himself and built huge walls around Syracuse.
  • His engineers built some of the first catapults, which he used to take the Carthaginian island fortress of Motya in 397 BCE.
  • He survived a Carthaginian siege of Syracuse in 396 BCE, when plague struck the besiegers.
  • He took Greek cities in southern Italy and sent ships into the Adriatic.

He also wanted fame as a writer, and one of his tragedies won a prize in Athens shortly before his death. Plato visited his court and left on bad terms. The story of the sword of Damocles is told about him.
